CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  February 1, 2021 - 2:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 2:04 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Wilson.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Brenda Harvey Williams presented a PowerPoint presentation
  highlighting the City's Black History Month festivities, which will be
  held as virtual celebrations due to COVID-19, throughout February
  2021; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Hampton asked staff to work with the Pasadena
  Convention Center and the Better Business Bureau to promote
  black-owned businesses in the City.

  Councilmember Kennedy reported that the California Institute of
  Technology (Caltech) announced that the university is publicly and
  unambiguously repudiating any affiliation with eugenics and the
  Human Betterment Foundation, and will rename campus buildings
  that are associated with the foundation or former leaders of Caltech
  that were engaged in the practicing of eugenics. He thanked
  Caltech board of trustees, President, and all involved for their
  actions in racial justice. He asked that staff disseminate information
  on the Pasadena Sister City, Dakar speaker series presenting
  Professor Danielle Wiggins of Caltech.

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke on the January 29, 2021 hosted virtual
  dedication that took place at Caltech in honor of the Tianqiao and
  Chrissy Chen Neuroscience Research Building (CNRB). He also
  asked staff to reach out to Dr. Steve Mayo, a prominent biologist at
  Caltech who may provide assistance for the City's vaccination
  event.

Council Minutes  1  02/01/2021
   Mayor Gordo requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory
  of those that have suffered due to death and illness caused by
  COVID-19 in Pasadena, the nation and around the world .

CONSENT CALENDAR  ECONOMIC  DEVELOPMENT  AND  TECHNOLOGY
  COMMITTEE: APPROVAL OF HOUSING ACQUISITION LOAN
  AGREEMENT WITH HERITAGE HOUSING PARTNERS TO
  PROVIDE PURCHASE FINANCING IN AN AMOUNT NOT-TO-
  EXCEED $607,500 TO IMPLEMENT PURCHASE OPTIONS ON
  AFFORDABLE HOMEOWNERSHIP UNITS AT 588 N. FAIR
  OAKS AVENUE, #1-03 #101 AND 106 E. SUMMIT ORANGE
  GROVE BOULEVARD, #304
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council take
  the following actions:
  (1) Find that the proposed housing financing and acquisition
  activity, as described in the agenda report, does not have a
  significant effect on the environment and has been determined to
  be categorically exempt under Class 26 (Acquisition of Housing) of
  the State California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") and,
  specifically, Section 15326 of the State CEQA Guidelines;
  (2) Approve a budget amendment appropriating $607,500 from
  the lnclusionary Housing Fund Unappropriated Fund Balance to the
  Housing Department's Fiscal Year (FY) 2021 Operating Budget for
  the HHP Housing Acquisition Project; (Budget Amendment No.
  2021-26)
  (3) Approve certain key business terms, as described in the
  agenda report, of the proposed Housing Acquisition Loan
  Agreement with Heritage Housing Partners; and
  (4) Authorize the City Manager to execute any and all documents
  necessary to effectuate the staff recommendation.

  Mayor Gordo noted that the agenda and staff report titles have been
  corrected to reflect the proper addresses for the proposed action ,
  which is located at, "588 N. Fair Oaks Avenue, #101 and 106 E.
  Orange Grove Boulevard , #304 ."

Council Minutes  2  02/01/2021
   Claim No. 13,672 James Eiler, Esq.,  25,000.00+
  Murchison & Cumming, LLP,
  representing Unified Parking
  Service, Inc.

  It was moved by Councilmember Kennedy, seconded by
  Councilmember Hampton, to approve all items on the Consent
  Calendar, including the correction to the agenda report related to
  Item 1 (Approval of Housing Acquisition Loan Agreement with
  Heritage Housing Partners) as detailed above:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS AND COMMENTS APPROVAL OF THE FEDERAL & STATE LEGISLATIVE
FROM COUNCIL  PLATFORMS FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2021
COMMITTEES  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is categorically exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) the general rule that CEQA
  only applies to projects that may have an effect on the environment;
  and
  (2) Approve the Federal Legislative Platform and the State
  Legislative Platform for calendar year 2021.
  Recommendation of the Legislative Policy Committee: At the
  January 26, 2021 meeting of the Legislative Policy Committee, staff
  presented both the Federal and State Legislative Platforms for
  calendar year 2021. In addition to the staff recommendations, the
  Committee agreed to include additional language regarding support
  for direct fiscal assistance to publicly owned utilities to credit
  delinquent utility bills for their customers during COVID-19. The
  Committee recommended forwarding both Platforms to the City
  Council for approval.

  Councilmember Madison, Chair of the Legislative Policy Committee
  (LPC), summarized the Committee's discussion; noting the
  dialogue with staff related to needed fiscal assistance for utility
  customers during the COVID-19 pandemic; and the Committee's
  action to forward the item to the City Council for consideration.
  Mayor Gordo, member of LPC, reported that the Committee
  discussed housing legislation, specifically related to local control.

  Julie Gutierrez, Assistant City Manager, provided introductory
  comments, and Jennifer Guess, Management Analyst IV,
  presented a PowerPoint on the item, and responded to questions.

Council Minutes  3  02/01/2021
   Councilmember Kennedy asked the Legislative Policy Committee
  to consider discussing the issue of water contaminants that may be
  present in the City's water sources. He also asked the City Council
  to review the City of Atlanta's issuance of $50 million housing bond
  for affordable housing.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, read aloud comments expressing
  concerns on Senate Bills: SB 9- Housing Development; SB 15 -
  Housing Development; SB50 - Planning and Zoning, and SB51 -
  California Competes Tax Credit from the following individuals:

  Nina Chomsky, Pasadena resident
  Christopher Sutton, Pasadena resident

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided information on the items
  that will be discussed at the February 22, 2021 City Council
  meeting, which will include a discussion on the City's General Plan ,
  Specific Plans, and the Housing Element; and responded to
  questions.

  Vice Mayor Wilson asked staff to provide additional information on
  legislation related to housing issues at the February 22, 2021 City
  Council meeting. Mayor Gordo requested that staff provide a brief
  report on the housing legislation bills referenced in the staff report,
  at the February 22, 2021 City Council meeting, and forward to the
  Legislative Policy Committee for further discussion.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Madison,
  seconded by Councilmember Hampton, to approve the staff
  recommendation:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

ORDINANCE - ADOPTED  ADOPT "AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF PASADENA
  AMENDING TITLE 2, CHAPTER 2.45, SECTION 2.45.050
  (VACATION OF DISTRICT APPOINTMENTS BY NEWLY
  ELECTED  COUNCILMEMBER)  OF  THE  PASADENA
  MUNICIPAL  CODE  TO  EXTEND  TO  MAYORAL
  APPOINTMENTS" (Introduced by Councilmember Madison)
  (Ordinance No. 7370)

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that public comment was received on
  items not on the agenda related to police oversight, which were
  distributed to the City Council and staff but will not be read aloud.

Council Minutes  4  02/01/2021
   Councilmember Hampton stated his preference that public
  comments that are on items not on the agenda be posted on the
  City's website.

  The above ordinance was adopted by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

INFORMATION ITEMS  PREDEVELOPMENT PLAN REVIEW OF A COMMERCIAL
  BUILDING PROPOSED AT 758 & 766 SOUTH FAIR OAKS
  AVENUE (HUNTINGTON HOSPITAL)
  Recommendation: This report is intended to provide information
  to the City Council; no action is required.

  David Reyes, Director of Planning and Community Development,
  provided introductory comments, and Beilin Yu, Senior Planner,
  presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, and responded
  to questions.

  Vice Mayor Wilson expressed concerns regarding potential vehicle
  and traffic impacts that might occur given the close proximity this
  project has to a number of adjacent medical office buildings.

  Dr. Lori Morgan, President of Huntington Hospital, provided
  information on the proposed project's medical offices, and Brad
  McCoy, Vice President of Construction of Huntington Hospital,
  presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, and responded
  to questions.

  Councilmember Williams voiced support of the Preliminary
  Consultation Design Review comments, referenced in Attachment
  B of the staff report; spoke on the need for a connection to the
  Fillmore Gold Line train station in terms of landscaping, streetscape
  etc., in connecting the building on the east side to fulfill some of the
  Specific Plan goals in making the area more walkable. She spoke
  on the need for staff to provide a cumulative impact report on the
  590 South Fair Oaks Avenue project.

  Vice Mayor Wilson asked staff to look at the surrounding area
  collectively as the construction reinvigorates a whole section of Fair
  Oaks Avenue as opposed to individual projects. He expressed
  concerns with the scale of the setback for the driveway drop-off as
  the area should be more pedestrian friendly.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

Council Minutes  5  02/01/2021
   CITY COUNCIL STUDY SESSION  ON  CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) AND LOCAL
  MOBILITY ANALYSIS (OUTSIDE CEQA)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council, as part
  of a study session, receive the oral report and information regarding
  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and Local Mobility
  Analysis, formerly referred to as Outside CEQA analysis.

  Mayor Gordo provided introductory comments; City Manager
  Mermell provided information from the November 16, 2020 City
  Council action in adopting an update to the City's California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) baseline, and direction to staff
  to provide in-depth information; and responded to questions.

  Laura Cornejo, Director of Transportation, provided introductory
  comments, and John Muggridge and Nico Boyd representing Fehr
  & Peers (City consultants), presented a PowerPoint presentation on
  the City's current transportation analysis framework, information on
  CEQA and Local Mobility processes; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Masuda requested information regarding the
  results of an online poll taken at a recent Transportation Advisory
  Committee (TAC) meeting.

  Conrad Viana, Transportation Engineer, provided information on
  the three tier thresholds that trigger a transportation review; and
  responded to questions.

  Councilmember Williams requested clarification and a flow chart on
  the levels and criteria of analysis that City projects are subject to
  regardless of the number of units. She also asked staff to provide a
  breakdown on the number of projects that triggered mitigations (as
  was represented in the PowerPoint presentation) between CEQA
  and Local Mobility. In addition, Councilmember Williams spoke on
  the need to collect cell phoneNehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) data to
  determine travel information when considering all projects in the
  City.

  Vice Mayor Wilson asked staff to provide information on best
  practices when considering cumulative impacts in relation to Local
  Mobility analysis.

  Councilmember Hampton spoke on the need for staff to collect
  more accurate, real-time, VMT data, and suggested that staff
  contact individuals in the surrounding area where a project will be
  built, and ask them to volunteer weekly VMT information as a
  possible data collection alternative.

Council Minutes  6  02/01/2021
   Mayor Gordo spoke on the community's frustration and feelings of
  disconnect related to City policies, development approvals, and the
  resulting traffic impacts. He spoke on the need for staff to review
  the City's mobility guidelines and seek out sufficient input from the
  community, as a solid approach to measuring the cumulative
  impacts of approved projects in the City.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that a number of letters and emails
  advocating for accurate analysis of traffic on City streets, the need
  for mitigation, and/or providing comments/suggestions, which were
  distributed to the City Council, posted on-line, and made part of the
  public record from the following individuals:

  Megan Foker, on behalf of Livable Pasadena
  Erika Foy, representing Protecting Pasadena
  Keep Pasadena Moving

  City Clerk Jomsky read aloud comments advocating for accurate
  analysis of traffic on City streets, the need for mitigation, increase
  of street safety measures, and/or providing comments/suggestions
  on the matter from the following individuals:

  Keep Pasadena Moving
  Ken Perry, Pasadena resident
  Avram Dean Gold, Pasadena resident
  Topher Mathers, Pasadena resident
  Erika Foy, Pasadena resident

  The City Council thanked staff and their consultants on their
  excellent work on such a difficult subject matter.

  Ms. Cornejo stated that per City Council direction, staff will return at
  a future meeting (March 2021) on the recommendation to award a
  contract to a consultant to assist the City in developing updated
  local mobility guidelines; followed by an update on the local mobility
  analysis process, and a potential path forward allowing the City
  Council to consider stricter CEQA thresholds.

  Councilmember Williams spoke on the need for staff to develop a
  process for updating the City's mobility element that would trigger a
  different kind of analysis or expand the tiers on the current analysis
  of projects.

  City Manager Mermell informed the City Council that staff will
  present the City's General Plan and Specific Plans for discussion at
  a future City Council meeting, and that staff will also discuss the
  impacts of the mobility plan and provide some context to the City
  Council as part of that same discussion.

Council Minutes  7  02/01/2021
   Councilmember Kennedy requested that staff respond to the public
  comments submitted by Ken Perry as he has continually engaged
  and continues to express displeasure with staff's actions on the
  matter.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  City Clerk Jomsky announced that a special City Council meeting
  will be held on Thursday, February 4, 2021, at 6:00 p.m., for the
  purpose of conducting qualified applicant interviews, and providing
  the City Council with the opportunity to select an appointee to fill the
  vacancy on the City Council, representing Council District 5.

  Councilmember Kennedy, Commissioner on the Burbank-
  Glendale-Pasadena Airport Authority Board, summarized the
  discussion of their meeting held earlier in the day.

ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the special meeting of the City Council
  adjourned at 5:29 p.m. in memory of all those that are ill and have
  lost th · lives during the COVID-19 pandemic.

  Victor M. Gord ,
  City of Pasadena
